text: Which oocyte-specific genes (single-cell) have no detectable mRNA in testis?
plan: Cell type category (scRNA): Oocytes / Cell type enriched AND Tissue category (RNA): Testis / Not detected
understanding: The question asks for genes that show specific expression in oocytes based on single-cell RNA sequencing data and have no detectable mRNA expression in testis based on tissue RNA data.

trail.why: The requirement asks for oocyte-specific genes in single-cell data, which corresponds to selecting 'Oocytes' at Level 1 and the specificity category 'Cell type enriched' (at least four-fold higher mRNA level compared to any other cell type) at Level 2.

The requirement specifies no detectable mRNA in testis, which corresponds to selecting 'testis' at Level 1 and 'Not detected' (defined as below the detection cut-off of 1 nTPM in the selected tissue) at Level 2.

requirements.why: It defines specificity and distribution across single cell types using scRNA-seq, which matches the single-cell specificity in oocytes.
It measures tissue-level RNA specificity and distribution across human tissues including testis, where 'Not detected' can be selected.
